title: Align WebSearch tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all WebSearch improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go WebSearch has the public tool name, query/domain parameters, deferred-discovery metadata, stricter domain-list guards, and partial helper-level work for citation formatting, normalized result blocks, policy objects, and an injectable server-tool provider. It is not yet runtime-equivalent to the TS reference. The TS tool is a provider-native Anthropic web_search_20250305 server-tool flow inside a single model API call, with provider/model enablement, passthrough permission suggestions, streaming server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result progress, usage accounting, and a query/results/duration output object. The Go tool still defaults to a local DuckDuckGo-style pipeline, registers unconditionally, uses a stateful local cache, cannot express or parse the Anthropic server-tool protocol in the common provider/types layer, emits different progress and error lifecycles, and returns a different model-facing result shape.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Go production execution defaults to local DDG search instead of the TS Anthropic web_search server tool
improvement_points.description: TS constructs an Anthropic-defined web_search_20250305 tool schema, injects it through extraToolSchemas, and asks the model/API to perform search inside the streaming API call. Go has a WebSearchServerToolProvider scaffold, but NewWebSearchTool defaults to local_fallback, registry_setup.go only registers that default instance, and no production code wires SetWebSearchServerToolProvider. The common provider Params/ToolDefinition surface only supports ordinary client tools, so it cannot currently send the TS extra server-tool schema without a provider/type extension.

improvement_points.title: Go provider/types cannot round-trip server_tool_use, web_search_tool_result, or web search usage
improvement_points.description: TS relies on Anthropic streaming content blocks server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result, including input_json_delta parsing and server_tool_use.web_search_requests usage. Go's Anthropic stream converter recognizes only text/tool_use/thinking blocks and Usage only contains token/cache fields. Unknown blocks can be preserved when deserializing stored messages, but the live Anthropic stream path drops unknown server-side block variants rather than preserving raw JSON or converting them into first-class WebSearch events.

improvement_points.title: Go adds a local WebSearch result cache that TS does not have and cached hits change output semantics
improvement_points.description: TS WebSearch does not have a tool-local result cache; each call builds a server-tool schema and invokes queryModelWithStreaming. Go uses a 15-minute searchCache keyed by query and domain filters. On cache hit it manufactures a single result with title 'Cached result', URL 'cache://websearch', and snippet containing the previous formatted output, then emits that as if it were a real search result. This changes freshness, citations, source URLs, result counts, and progress behavior.

improvement_points.title: Go's model-facing and internal output shape does not match TS query/results/durationSeconds semantics
improvement_points.description: TS call returns an Output object with query, results array, and durationSeconds. Search result objects include tool_use_id and content entries with title/url only; mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam converts that into a text block with Links JSON and the sources reminder. Go directly returns types.ToolResult.Content plus ContentBlocks and Metadata, has no durationSeconds or search-count result object, lacks tool_use_id on WebSearchToolResultBlock, includes snippets in Links JSON, and returns plain 'No results found.' without the TS header/reminder path.

improvement_points.title: Server-tool errors are surfaced as TS result strings but Go falls through to local search
improvement_points.description: TS treats a web_search_tool_result whose content is an error object as a successful tool call containing the string 'Web search error: <error_code>' in results. Go runWebSearchServerTool converts ErrorCode into an error, and Execute ignores non-unavailable server-tool errors before continuing to providerSearch/local fallback. That can mask upstream web_search failures, return unrelated local DDG results, and lose the TS error string.

improvement_points.title: Go progress events are not emitted at the same lifecycle points or with the same data as TS
improvement_points.description: TS progress is derived from streamed server_tool_use input_json_delta and web_search_tool_result block starts. It emits query_update only when the server tool query is known/changed and search_results_received with resultCount and the actual query. Go emits started/query_update before full validation and before policy checks, omits the query from search_results_received, emits fake received-results events for cache hits, and the provider-native serverTool branch currently returns without emitting search_results_received at all.

improvement_points.title: Go lacks TS provider/model enablement and WebSearch-specific permission suggestion behavior
improvement_points.description: TS WebSearch is only exposed when the active API provider/model supports it and checkPermissions returns a passthrough decision with a localSettings allow-rule suggestion. tools.ts also filters denied tools before applying isEnabled. Go registers WebSearch unconditionally in SetupRegistry, has no per-tool isEnabled method in the Tool interface, and relies on a generic permission handler that only receives ToolName/Input without WebSearch-specific passthrough message or localSettings suggestion data.

improvement_points.title: WebSearch request usage is not tracked in Go session usage or cost state
improvement_points.description: TS carries server_tool_use.web_search_requests through API usage normalization, modelUsage, cost tracking, stats, and session summaries. Go's Usage type and session accumulation only account for tokens/cache fields. Because the local fallback is not an Anthropic server tool and the provider layer cannot parse server_tool_use usage, Go cannot display or cost web search request counts like TS.

improvement_points.title: Input schema strictness and validation error text/codes differ
improvement_points.description: TS publishes a strict zod object with query min(2), optional string arrays, and validateInput returns exact messages and numeric errorCode values for missing query and allowed/blocked conflict. Go's schema has no minLength/additionalProperties equivalent, parseInput ignores unknown JSON fields, Execute trims query and returns different user-visible messages without error codes, and it emits progress before conflict validation.

improvement_points.title: Go tests cover helpers and known gaps more than the production TS-equivalent path
improvement_points.description: The current Go suite has useful helper tests for local fallback, normalization, citations, cache keys, policy, and fake server providers, but it does not fail on the absence of a production server-tool provider, extraToolSchemas request shape, beta header emission, live stream server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result parsing, web_search_requests usage, exact output object/duration behavior, or default registry enablement. Some alignment comments are stale relative to the current TS code, so the suite can give a stronger parity signal than the production path deserves.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add provider/types support for Anthropic-defined web_search server-tool protocol
acceptance_criteria: provider.Params can carry Anthropic-defined extra tool schemas such as {type:'web_search_20250305', name:'web_search', allowed_domains, blocked_domains, max_uses}.
Anthropic request construction emits the web_search_20250305 server tool and web-search-2025-03-05 beta header where TS does.
Streaming and non-streaming Anthropic responses preserve/convert server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result blocks without dropping unknown server-side data.
types.Usage carries server_tool_use.web_search_requests without breaking existing token/cache usage callers.
No ordinary Go client tool is accidentally serialized as an Anthropic-defined server tool.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire WebSearchTool to the provider-native server tool in production registry/query lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: A default WebSearch registered by SetupRegistry uses the provider-native web_search_20250305 path when the active provider/model supports TS WebSearch.
allowed_domains and blocked_domains are passed to the server tool before search rather than only post-filtered after a local search.
Local DDG search is not the default production path; if retained, it is explicitly gated as an unavailable-provider fallback that cannot mask server-tool errors.
WebSearch uses the request context/abort lifecycle rather than a separate fixed local-only timeout when running provider-native search.
The existing local fallback gap test is either removed or inverted to assert provider_native parity.

implementation_subtasks.title: Remove or make TS-compatible the local WebSearch cache lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Repeated WebSearch calls do not return synthetic cache://websearch citations.
If any cache remains, cached data preserves the original result list/URLs and is disabled for provider-native server-tool calls unless TS has equivalent behavior.
No results are cached as already formatted model-facing strings.
Tests prove same query/domain filters either triggers fresh provider-native execution or returns byte-for-byte equivalent original source URLs.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align WebSearch output, citation formatting, empty result, duration, and server error rendering
acceptance_criteria: Go can represent the TS Output shape: query, results array of strings/search result objects, and durationSeconds.
Search result objects preserve tool_use_id and Links JSON contains only title/url unless TS source behavior changes.
Empty results still flow through the TS-style header/reminder path instead of plain 'No results found.' when a WebSearch call completes.
web_search_tool_result error envelopes render as 'Web search error: <error_code>' result strings and are not silently replaced by local fallback results.
Result UI/metadata can derive TS-equivalent search count and duration.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align WebSearch progress events with TS streamed server-tool lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: No progress event is emitted for inputs that fail validation before TS would call the tool.
query_update is emitted from the actual server_tool_use query stream, including changed query text.
search_results_received includes both resultCount and query with TS-compatible naming and values.
Provider-native success emits search_results_received exactly when web_search_tool_result arrives.
Cache/fallback paths do not emit misleading fake server-tool progress.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement TS-compatible WebSearch enablement and permission suggestion metadata
acceptance_criteria: WebSearch is hidden/disabled for providers and models where TS WebSearchTool.isEnabled() returns false.
Blanket deny rules prevent WebSearch from being visible before model tool selection, matching TS getTools filtering.
Permission checks can return a WebSearch passthrough decision with the TS message and a localSettings addRules suggestion for {toolName:'WebSearch'}.
Generic permission behavior for other tools is unchanged.

implementation_subtasks.title: Track server_tool_use.web_search_requests through Go usage, cost, and session state
acceptance_criteria: Go Usage includes a server-tool-use bucket with web_search_requests.
Anthropic provider stream and non-stream fallback copy web_search request counts from API usage.
Session usage/status/cost surfaces include web search request counts where TS reports them.
Existing token/cache usage behavior and tests remain unchanged.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align WebSearch schema strictness and validation diagnostics
acceptance_criteria: Go WebSearch schema expresses query min length and rejects unknown fields when the TS strict object would reject them.
Missing query and allowed/blocked conflict return TS-compatible messages and machine-readable error codes or equivalent metadata.
One-character query behavior is covered and matches the TS schema/validation path selected by the runtime.
Progress callbacks are not fired before validation failures.

implementation_subtasks.title: Replace WebSearch helper-only parity tests with production-path conformance fixtures
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert the real Go production path emits the Anthropic server-tool request shape including beta header, max_uses, and domain filters.
Stream fixtures cover server_tool_use input_json_delta, web_search_tool_result success, web_search_tool_result error envelopes, and usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests.
The current local_fallback gap test is retired or inverted once provider-native parity lands.
Stale comments in WebSearch alignment tests are updated so failures represent current known gaps, not already-fixed historical ones.
Fixtures compare TS normalized output against Go normalized output for success, error, empty result, allowed_domains, blocked_domains, and validation failures.
WebSearch input validation and schema behavior match the original TS implementation for all report gaps.
WebSearch model-visible output and structured result data match TS golden fixtures.
WebSearch runtime side effects, state transitions, permission decisions, and error branches listed in improvement_points are implemented or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.
All implementation_subtasks acceptance criteria are satisfied.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
